category_title: Non-dominant students with low displays of aggression
minimal_context: The student is working in a collaborative group during science class on a storytelling activity about being taken away by aliens.
dialogue:
TUTOR: For today's science class, please work in your collaborative groups and imagine how we will feel if the aliens came and took us away from our homes and families and put us in cages.

STUDENT: I don't want him in my group. I am not doing anything but he comes and starts to yell at you, and he fights with everyone.

TUTOR: Please just try to focus on the activity with your group members.

STUDENT: But he isn't doing the work. He is just sitting there and was very sad like he was going to start crying about his old home.

TUTOR: What do you think you should say to him?

STUDENT: They still tell you bad things all the time and tell you nicknames, so if he is going to cry, we are just going to tease him.

options.A: Suggest that the student call on a neighbor, ask a friend, or poll the collaborative group for help.
options.B: Allow the student to retain their initial inferences about their peer without correcting them during the activity.
options.C: Encourage the student to identify their previous experiences and conceptions regarding the topic through the storytelling activity.
options.D: Provide specific feedback and guiding questions that force the student to link their narrative elements to physical evidence.
